content: Ibuprofen is an oral medication classified as a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID). It is commonly used for its analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties. The drug is FDA-approved for the treatment of conditions such as fever, headache, migraine, osteoarthritis, pain, primary dysmenorrhea, and rheumatoid arthritis. Common Adverse Reactions Adverse effects associated with ibuprofen use include hypotension, rash, hypernatremia, hypoalbuminemia, hypoproteinemia, elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) levels, flatulence, nausea, vomiting, heartburn, thrombocytosis, bacteremia, dizziness, headache, elevated serum blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and bacterial pneumonia. Adult Indications and Dosage Non-prescription dosing: The recommended dose is 200 to 400 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours as needed, with a maximum daily dose of 1200 mg. Ibuprofen should not be taken for more than 10 days unless directed by a physician. The smallest effective dose should always be used. Osteoarthritis: The dosage range is 1200 to 3200 mg daily, divided into doses of 300 mg four times daily or 400 mg, 600 mg, or 800 mg three to four times daily. Sustained-release preparations (e.g., Ibu-Slo or Fenlong) at 600 mg twice daily are as effective as regular-release preparations at 400 mg three times daily. Rheumatoid arthritis: Patients often respond better to higher doses, with a recommended range of 1200 to 3200 mg daily, divided into multiple doses. Pediatric Indications and Dosage Fever (age 17 years and older): 400 mg intravenously every 4 to 6 hours, or alternatively, 100 to 200 mg IV every 4 hours. The infusion should last at least 30 minutes. Oral suspension (age 6 months to 2 years): Dosage depends on weight and age, administered every 6 to 8 hours as needed. For example: 12 to 17 pounds (6 to 11 months): 50 mg per dose. 18 to 23 pounds (12 to 23 months): 75 mg per dose. Maximum: 4 doses per day. Oral suspension (age 2 years and older): Dosage also depends on weight and age, administered every 6 to 8 hours as needed. For example: 24 to 35 pounds (2 to 3 years): 100 mg per dose. 36 to 47 pounds (4 to 5 years): 150 mg per dose. 48 to 59 pounds (6 to 8 years): 200 mg per dose. 60 to 71 pounds (9 to 10 years): 250 mg per dose. 72 to 95 pounds (11 years): 300 mg per dose. Maximum: 4 doses per day. Oral tablets (age 12 years and older): 200 to 400 mg orally every 4 to 6 hours as needed, with a maximum daily dose of 1200 mg. Warnings and Precautions Allergy alert: Ibuprofen may cause severe allergic reactions, particularly in individuals allergic to aspirin. Symptoms include hives, facial swelling, asthma (wheezing), shock, skin reddening, rash, and blisters. If an allergic reaction occurs, discontinue use immediately and seek medical attention. Stomach bleeding warning: Ibuprofen, as an NSAID, may cause severe stomach bleeding. The risk is higher in individuals aged 60 or older, those with a history of stomach ulcers or bleeding problems, those taking anticoagulants or steroid drugs, those consuming three or more alcoholic drinks daily, or those taking the medication for longer than directed. Heart attack and stroke risk: The risk of heart attack or stroke may increase with prolonged use or doses exceeding the recommended amount. Contraindications Do not use ibuprofen if you have had an allergic reaction to any pain reliever or fever reducer, or immediately before or after heart surgery. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding Ibuprofen should not be used during the last three months of pregnancy unless specifically directed by a physician, as it may cause complications for the unborn child or during delivery. Consult a healthcare professional before use if pregnant or breastfeeding. Administration and Monitoring Ibuprofen can be administered orally or intravenously. When taken orally, it should be taken with food or milk to minimize stomach upset. Monitoring for adverse effects, particularly gastrointestinal and cardiovascular symptoms, is recommended. Storage Store ibuprofen at 20-25°C (68-77°F) and avoid excessive heat above 40°C (104°F). Overdose In case of overdose, seek immediate medical attention or contact a Poison Control Center. Brand Names Common brand names for ibuprofen include Advil, Motrin, A-G Profen, Addaprin, Bufen, Genpril, Caldolor, and Haltran. This information is intended for educational purposes and should not replace professional medical advice. Always consult a healthcare provider for guidance specific to your condition.
